Subject: Retention: rollback bridge, escrow sequencing & subprocessor onboarding

Hi Elena / NovusCare contracts team,

Thanks again for taking time yesterday. To keep things moving for the DPA v3 redlines, we need to align on two operational points before we sign:

1) Backup purge sequencing: NovusCare asked for a 30-day backup purge window in section 4.2 of your redline. Can you confirm whether that refers to primary live backups only or includes offsite snapshots and cross-region replication?

2) Escrow/rollback bridge: we need clarity on the escrow handoff window in the event of a contractual exit — specifically the sequencing between providing immutable snapshots to a third‑party escrow and our scheduled retention purge. We're proposing a short hold (7 calendar days) between escrow transfer and purge to allow integrity checks.

3) Subprocessor onboarding: we have a standard subprocessor checklist (SOC attestation, dataflow map, access controls). If NovusCare prefers an additional approval step for new subprocessor onboarding, let's capture that in an annex.

Attached: highlighted redlines and a proposed backup snapshot timeline (CSV).

Can you please: (a) confirm whether the 30-day purge includes offsite snapshots, (b) confirm acceptance of a 7-day escrow integrity hold, and (c) indicate whether you need a formal onboarding approval step for subprocessors?

If easier, happy to jump on a 30-minute call with Samir and your security lead this week.

Thanks,

Camila Reyes
Senior Manager, Customer Security Ops
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Retention: rollback bridge, escrow sequencing & subprocessor onboarding

Camila —

Thanks for the clear summary. Quick answers below:

- The 30-day purge in our redline was intended to apply to customer-facing backups and operational snapshots, not long-term offsite archival copies. That said, our platform team requires a short overlap window for cross-region replication to finish; typical window is 48–72 hours.

- We are open to the 7-day escrow integrity hold, provided we receive a cryptographic checksum and transfer manifest within 24 hours of the escrow handoff.

- For subprocessors: NovusCare legal prefers an approval step for any new subprocessor that will hold primary customer data. We can accept a lightweight notice-and-objection process with a 14-calendar-day objection window.

I can put Samir on this thread for the technical details (replication windows, log retention). When would you be available for a quick call?

Best,
Elena Morales
Sr. Counsel, Data & Privacy
NovusCare

Camila / team,

Thanks — copying what I'd propose operationally so we can give NovusCare concrete options:

Option A (conservative):
- Backups & operational snapshots: retain for 30 days. Purge job runs daily, retention calculation based on createtime; cross-region replicas are tagged and will be purged 72 hours after primary purge to allow replication completion.
- Escrow handoff: freeze purge for 7 days post-handoff; provide SHA256 checksums and transfer manifest within 24 hours.
- Subprocessor onboarding: implement notice-and-objection (14 days) for subprocessors with access to primary customer data.

Option B (customer-friendly):
- Backups & snapshots: 90-day retention for offsite snapshots, 30-day for operational restore points. Purge job staged in two phases: (1) delete operational restore points, (2) mark offsite snapshots for quarantine and physical deletion after 90 days.
- Escrow: same as above.

Operational impacts: Option B increases storage and snapshot egress cost ~1.8x for the NovusCare workload unless we apply tiered compression and differential snapshots. If they want us to accept the 30-day redline strictly for everything, we'll need a clause allowing for cross-region replication grace (72 hrs) and an exception for escrow integrity checks.

Attaching a quick CSV timeline for the two options. If NovusCare wants the 30-day clause as-is, we should ask legal to include an explicit replication grace and escrow manifest SLA.

-Karthik
Director, Platform Ops
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: backup_snapshot_timeline.csv]

Elena — thanks for the quick turn.

We can accept the notice-and-objection flow for subprocessors (14 days). Regarding backups: to avoid ambiguity in the DPA, we'd prefer to add two short definitions and one grace clause:

Definitions to add to the DPA:
- "Operational restore points": backups intended for short-term restore operations (retain 30 days).
- "Offsite snapshots": cross-region immutable snapshots stored for longer-term recovery (retain 90 days unless otherwise agreed).

Grace clause: 
- "Cross-region replication grace": in the event of cross-region replication, Redwood will allow up to 72 hours after the retention cutoff for replicas to catch up prior to deletion.

Escrow: we accept the 7-day hold. We'll provide SHA256 checksums and a transfer manifest within 24 hours of handoff. We'll also include an appendix that maps the escrow handoff steps to technical artifacts (manifest, snapshot IDs, storage URIs).

If that matches NovusCare's expectations, please confirm and we will ask Contracts to prepare a clean DPA for signature with the minor annexes. We can push DocuSign to complete within 72 hours of your confirmation.

Regards,
Olga Petrov
Head of Compliance, Redwood Inference
[Attachment referenced: NovusCare_DPA_v3_redlines.pdf]
